fact: Boyd Lake Shores First Filing's amended covenants, recorded in Larimer County on April 11, 2002, let no landscaping be installed or altered on a lot until the Architectural Control Committee approves in writing a landscaping plan showing its nature, type, height and location, and list landscaping, screening, trellises and patio covers among the changes that need approval in advance.
quote: No landscaping shall be installed on any lot, or altered thereafter, unless a landscaping plan showing the nature, type, height, and location of the proposed landscaping improvements has been submitted to and approved by the Architectural Review Board in writing. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, prior approval of the Architectural Review Board must be obtained for any of the following: (i) attachments to the exterior of a structure, (ii) installation of greenhouses, (iii) installation of patio covers, landscaping, screening, trellises and the like, (iv) change in exterior paint colors, (v) installation of any barn corral, shed or storage building, and (vi) any other exterior change, including cosmetic changes such as garage doors, shutters and the like.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 4.1 (recorded April 11, 2002, Larimer County Reception No. 2002040630)
notes: Read from the recorded scan (page 7) on 2026-09-26; the scan has no text layer, so the quote was read from the page image and matches the HOA's web transcription at https://boydlakeshores.com/covenants. Sec. 2.3 defines the Architectural Review Board as the Architectural Control Committee created under Article V.

fact: The First Filing's covenants let the Architectural Control Committee judge materials and workmanship, harmony with existing structures, placement against topography and finished ground elevation, and approve an improvement only if it fits its surroundings and its upkeep will not burden the association, with conditions if it chooses.
quote: The authority of the Architectural Review Board shall extend to the quality, workmanship and materials for any structure proposed; conformity and harmony of exterior design and finish with existing structures within the subdivision; location of all structures with respect to the existing buildings, topography and finished ground elevation; and all other matters required to assure that such structures enhance the quality of the subdivision and are erected in accordance with the plan for the subdivision. … The ACC shall approve any proposed improvement to property only if it deems in its reasonable discretion that the improvement to property in the location indicated will not be detrimental to the appearance of the surrounding areas of the development as a whole; that the appearance of the proposed improvement to property will be in harmony with the surrounding areas of the development area; that the improvement to property will not detract from the beauty, wholesomeness and attractiveness of the development area or the enjoyment thereof by Owners; and that the upkeep and maintenance of the proposed improvement to property will not become a burden on the Association. The ACC may condition its approval of any proposed improvement to property upon the making of such changes therein as the ACC may deem appropriate.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Secs. 4.1 and 5.4 (recorded April 11, 2002, Larimer County Reception No. 2002040630)
notes: Pages 7 to 9 of the recorded scan, read from the page images on 2026-09-26.

fact: Section 3.12 of the First Filing's covenants requires all landscaping, including grass, to be irrigated, trimmed and maintained in good condition at all times.
quote: All lots shall at all times be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition, and no litter or debris shall be deposited or allowed to accumulate on any lot. All landscaping, including grass, shall be irrigated, trimmed and maintained in good condition at all times.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 3.12, Unsightly Uses (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 5 of the recorded scan.

fact: The First Filing's 2002 amended covenants never mention artificial turf, synthetic grass or putting greens (read September 26, 2026).
quote: Read in full on September 26, 2026: Articles I through VII of the Amended Declaration (Reception No. 2002040630) in the HOA's web transcription, checked against the recorded scan. None contains "turf", "artificial", "synthetic" or "putting"; the only grass lines are Sec. 3.12's "All landscaping, including grass, shall be irrigated, trimmed and maintained in good condition at all times" and Sec. 3.25's duty to keep the lake-front park lot "planted with grass" or surfaced "with gravel or other suitable surfacing."
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores HOA, Covenants page: web transcription of the Amended Declaration of Covenants (04/11/2002) and the 2024 amendment to Sec. 3.16
notes: Honest NOT FOUND. The page carries the HOA's note that the web copy does not supersede the recorded document; the recorded scan (https://static.mywebsites360.com/f396386422a34a368cbd0f5bcc703bc9/r/fa321efc158343de9e998d62f6f0c221/1/Amended_Covenants_2002.pdf, 20 pages) has no text layer and was checked page by page for the sections cited. The HOA's posted ACC material also includes a creosote note (https://boydlakeshores.com/creosote-use-in-landscape) and no other landscape guidelines.

fact: Under the First Filing's covenants an applicant submits whatever descriptions, plot, drainage and landscaping plans, specifications and samples the committee reasonably requests, the committee may postpone review until it has them all, and it must try to decide in writing within 30 days after that, stating its reasons for any denial.
quote: Prior to commencement of work requiring ACC action, the person proposing to take such an action to Property, "Applicant" shall submit to the ARB at its offices, such description, surveys, plot plans, drainage plans, elevation drawings, landscaping plans, construction plans, specifications and samples of materials and colors as the ACC shall reasonably request showing the nature, kind, shape, height, width, color, materials, and location of the proposed improvement to property. Until receipt by the Architectural Review Board of all required materials in connection with the proposed improvement to property, the ACC may postpone review of any materials submitted for approval. … The ACC shall take reasonable steps to reach a decision within thirty (30) days after receipt by the ACC of all materials required by it for review. The decision shall be in writing and, if the decision is not to approve a proposed improvement to property, the reasons therefore shall be stated.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Secs. 5.3 and 5.7 (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Pages 9 and 10 of the recorded scan.

fact: The First Filing's covenants let the Architectural Control Committee set reasonable review fees in its guidelines or rules, uniform by project type or based on a project's cost.
quote: The ACC may, in its guidelines or rules, provide for payment of reasonable fees to accompany each request for approval of any proposed improvement to property. The Architectural Review Board may provide that the amount of such fees shall be uniform for similar types of proposed improvement to property, or the fees may be determined in any other reasonable manner, such as based upon the cost of the proposed improvement to property.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 5.6, Architectural Review Fees (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 9 of the recorded scan. No fee schedule is posted on the HOA site, and the posted application form (v05092017) has no fee line.

fact: Under the First Filing's covenants an owner gives the committee written notice of completion, the committee may inspect until 30 days after that notice, and work done without approval, not as approved or not completed within one year of approval must be remedied within 45 days of the committee's ruling.
quote: Promptly upon completion of the improvement to property, the applicant shall give written notice of completion to the ACC … the right of inspection shall terminate thirty (30) days after the ACC shall have received a notice of completion from the Applicant. … If, as a result of inspections or otherwise, the ACC finds that any improvement to property has been done without obtaining the approval of the ACC, or was not done in substantial compliance with the description and materials furnished by the Applicant to the ACC or was not completed within one year after the date of approval by the ACC, the ACC shall notify the applicant in writing of any noncompliance … If the ACC determines that a noncompliance exists, the Applicant shall remedy or remove the same within a period of not more than forty-five (45) days from the date of receipt by the Applicant of the ruling of the ACC.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Secs. 5.8, 5.9, 5.10 and 5.12 (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 10 of the recorded scan.

fact: The First Filing's covenants let an owner appeal a committee decision to the Board in writing within 30 days, and let the committee grant written variances, signed by a majority of its members, from rules on height, size or placement where topography, natural obstructions, hardship, aesthetic or environmental considerations call for it, without excusing government zoning or setback rules.
quote: The ACC may authorize variances from compliance with any of the provisions of this Declaration or any Supplemental Declaration, including restrictions upon height, size, floor area or placement of structures or similar restrictions, when circumstances such as topography, natural obstructions, under hardship, aesthetic or environmental considerations may require. Such variances must be evidenced in writing and shall become effective when signed by at least a majority of the members of the ACC. … nor shall the granting of the variance affect to any way the Owner's obligation to comply with all governmental laws and regulations affecting the Property concerned, including, but not limited to, zoning ordinances and setback lines or requirements imposed by any governmental authority having jurisdiction. … Any decision of the ACC may be appealed to the Board of Directors. Any appeal shall be made in writing to the Board within thirty (30) days of either the ACC or Board of Director's decision.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Secs. 5.13 and 5.20 (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Pages 11 and 12 of the recorded scan.

fact: The Boyd Lake Shores HOA's Architectural Control page says review takes 2 to 3 weeks and can take several rounds, and that owners must not start work before written approval and may face penalties if they do.
quote: Do not start work on your project before receiving ACC approval in writing.  Homeowners may be subject to penalties for performing work without ACC approval. … Important Note: Do not wait until the last minute to submit your ACC Review Application.   It can take several weeks to review an application and there may be several rounds of review before final approval of your project. ACC Review Process : (2-3 Weeks)
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores HOA, Architectural Control page (ACC project submission process)
notes: The page lists four ACC members by name (not reproduced) and links the application PDF.

fact: The First Filing's architectural review application lists landscaping and hardscaping among its project types, asks for color and material samples, manufacturers' brochures or links and full-size renderings of the changes on the lot, and has the owner acknowledge that association approval is not Larimer County approval and that a building permit may be required.
quote: This request is for the following type of improvement: Exterior Paint Windows Roofing Landscaping Outbuilding Room Addition Deck/Patio Hardscaping Major remodel Other: … Required attachments to application: Color Sample Full size renderings of changes/additions on lot Material Sample Manufacturers’ Brochure(s) or url Full size renderings of changes to structure(s) I understand that I must receive approval from the Association to proceed. I understand that Association approval does not constitute approval of Larimer County and that I may be required to obtain a building permit. I understand that my improvements must be completed per specifications or approval is withdrawn. I agree to send the Architectural Committee a Notice of Completion upon the completion of this improvement.
source_label: Boyd Lake Homeowners Association, 1st Filing, Application for Architectural Review (form version dated May 9, 2017)
notes: Two-page form, text layer extracted 2026-09-26. The form has no fee line. It also authorizes the committee to enter the property to evaluate the application.

fact: At the First Filing's 2022 annual meeting the board and committee told owners to submit landscaping changes such as added trees, said putting back the same things needs no application, and advised submitting whenever in doubt.
quote: Do we need to submit any approval for landscaping or colors of the house? - Board / ACC response : If changing the color, adding more trees, or any major structure changes you should submit those changes to the ACC. - Rule of thumb was that if you are going back with the same things no need to submit an application to the ACC. Also recommended to error on the side of caution, if you feel like your project needs approval submit an application just to be sure.
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores First Filing, 2022 Annual Board Meeting notes (posted with the 2022 board minutes)
notes: The question was asked by a named member (not reproduced). The notes record 27 of 42 in attendance.

fact: The First Filing association describes itself as self-managed, with volunteers reviewing committee plans, and reminds owners that landscaping changes must be approved by the committee before work starts.
quote: Please remember that if you do any remodeling to the exterior of your home or make changes to the landscaping these changes must be approved by the ACC prior to the commencement of work. … As you know there are numerous folks who move the dock, plant and water flowers, pay the bills, kill weeds, run HOA meetings, review ACC plans, etc. This is why our dues are low. We are a self-managed HOA with considerable volunteer involvement.
source_label: Boyd Lake Homeowners Association, First Filing, 2022 Annual Assessment Letter and Yearly Information (June 1, 2022)
notes: Posted with the 2022 board minutes.

fact: The Boyd Lake Shores Architectural Control Committee says no new landscape in the association should include creosote-coated timbers or other creosote materials, citing federal limits on creosote railroad ties and the risk of contaminating the lake.
quote: There have been questions to the ACC from Association Homeowners regarding the use of Creosote coated timbers in their landscaping plans.  Below are some findings that are shared here strictly as a convenience. No new Association Landscapes should include materials containing creosote based on the following: The EPA can't really regulate home owners, but they have stopped the availability of creosote ties, and forbid professional installation of such at residential sites. … so this is a good argument for concern with contamination of the lake
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores HOA, ACC page: Creosote Use In Landscape
notes: Undated ACC note; it links three EPA pages.

fact: The First Filing's covenants require houses on lots adjacent to Boyd Lake to be single-story dwellings.
quote: except for lots adjacent to Boyd Lake which shall be single story dwellings with a main floor area of not less than 1600 square feet exclusive of any garage of open porch
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 3.1 (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Pages 2 and 3 of the recorded scan.

fact: The First Filing's covenants let the Architectural Control Committee adopt guidelines on structures and materials, meant in part to guard the subdivision's natural beauty and to place structures so they block other owners' views as little as reasonably possible.
quote: The Architectural Control Committee may adopt Guidelines and Rules governing the type of structures to be permitted in the Subdivision, permitted construction materials and the like. These Guidelines and Rules are made for the purpose of creating and keeping the Subdivision, so far as possible, desirable, attractive, beneficial, uniform, harmonious, and suitable in architectural design, materials, and appearance; limiting the use of lots to single family residential buildings; guarding against unnecessary interference with the natural beauty of the Subdivision; locating structures on lots so as to minimize, to the extent reasonably possible, the obstruction of view of other Lot owners and prohibiting improper uses of adjoining properties in the Subdivision, all for the mutual benefits and protection of all owners.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 4.2 (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 8 of the recorded scan.

fact: In October 2019 the First Filing's board ruled that committee-drafted guidelines on where structures and some landscaping could go on lakeside lots went beyond what a guideline may do and would need a covenant change voted by all members.
quote: The ACC provided a set of guidelines to specify locations of structures and some landscaping focused on lake side lots. The BOD discussed this in some detail and ruled as follows: o The proposed guidelines suggested by the ACC go far beyond what is allowed as a guideline. Changes of this magnitude require a formal change to the covenants which will require a vote of all members. o The BOD does understand the ACC is working to fix shortcomings of the current covenants. The BOD is suggesting that changing the setback rules may solve the issues in a more straightforward and enforceable way.
source_label: Boyd Lake Homeowners Association, First Filing, Board of Directors meeting minutes, October 15, 2019
notes: The same minutes note 'recent issues with ACC landscaping approvals' prompting talk of covenant changes. No lakeside guidelines or covenant amendment on setbacks appear on the HOA site as of 2026-09-26; the only posted amendment is the 2024 rental change to Sec. 3.16.

fact: In October 2019 the First Filing's board said the covenants make no guarantee of lake views and that it would not reverse plantings the committee had approved.
quote: The BOD will respond … reiterating that the covenants make no guarantee for lake views and we won’t be reversing ACC approved plans for plantings.
source_label: Boyd Lake Homeowners Association, First Filing, Board of Directors meeting minutes, October 15, 2019
notes: The minutes name the owner who asked for trees to be removed; the name is left out here.

fact: The First Filing's board minutes of October 2019 say approving work on the Greeley and Loveland Irrigation Company's property along the lake is the board's responsibility, as when it approved adding rock to existing riprap against wave erosion.
quote: … Request for work on GLIC property • Approval for work in this area is the responsibility of the BOD. … agreed to write a letter approving the addition of rock to the existing rip-rap to protect against lake wave erosion.
source_label: Boyd Lake Homeowners Association, First Filing, Board of Directors meeting minutes, October 15, 2019
notes: GLIC is the Greeley and Loveland Irrigation Company (the HOA's recreation-rights page and the Larimer County parcel roll name it). The owner's name in the heading is left out.

fact: The Boyd Lake Shores HOA says it bought full-use recreation rights on Boyd Lake from the Greeley and Loveland Irrigation Company (GLIC) in 1972.
quote: As HOA members should be kept aware of developments surrounding the conflict of Boyd Lake State Park recreation rules and regulations with our full use recreation rights the HOA purchased from GLIC in 1972, the BOD will be posting relevant information on this page.
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores HOA, Boyd Lake Recreation Rights page
notes: The rest of the page concerns 2011 talks with Boyd Lake State Park about swimming and no-wake zones.

fact: The First Filing's covenants give every owner a perpetual private easement over Lot 10, Block 2, the lake-front park, to reach Boyd Lake for boating, swimming and related recreation.
quote: There is hereby granted to all of the Owners of all lots in Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing a perpetual, private easement upon Lot 10, Block 2, Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing for ingress and egress to Boyd Lake for the purposes of boating, swimming, and related recreational activities.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 3.25, Lake Front Park (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 7 of the recorded scan. The HOA's park-reservation page limits park bookings to First Filing members and says the boat ramp stays open to all members.

fact: The Boyd Lake Shores HOA says its neighborhood was the first housing development on the east side of Boyd Lake, developed from the late 1960s on.
quote: Boyd Lake Shores HOA 1 was the first housing development on the east side of Boyd Lake.  It was developed from the late 1960's until now.
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores HOA website, home page

fact: Boyd Lake Shores' original 1971 protective covenants cover Blocks 1 and 2 of a plat the Larimer County Planning Commission approved on August 13, 1963.
quote: That Trident, Inc., being the owner of Blocks 1 and 2, BOYD LAKE SHORES, a subdivision of a part of the East Half (E 1/2) of Section 5, Township S North, Range 68 West of the 6th Principal Meridian, County of Larimer and State of Colorado, As shown on the plat thereof approved by the Larimer County Planning Commission on the 13th day of August, 1963, does hereby make the following declarations
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores HOA, Original Covenants page: Protective Covenants, 1971 (web transcription)
notes: "Township S North" is the transcription's rendering of Township 5 North.

quote: SUBNAME: BOYD LAKE SHORES · SUBNUM: 0198 · RECEPTNUM: 851866 · MUNICIPALITY: LARIMER COUNTY … SUBNAME: BOYD LAKE SHORES 2ND · MUNICIPALITY: LARIMER COUNTY … SUBNAME: BOYD LAKE SHORES 3RD · MUNICIPALITY: LARIMER COUNTY

fact: The First Filing's covenants keep each house and accessory at least 40 feet from the front street, 25 feet from a side street and 10 feet from the nearest lot, and detached accessory buildings at least 75 feet from the front and 25 feet from all other lines, which the committee may adjust.
quote: Each single family detached dwelling and accessory shall be located at least 40 feet from the street at the front of the Lot and 25 feet from any side street; and at least 10 feet from the boundary of the nearest adjacent Lot. Accessory detached buildings shall be no closer than 75 feet to the front of the Lot and 25 feet from all other property lines. Anything herein notwithstanding the Architectural Control Committee shall have the right to allow or require adjustments to these setbacks as it determines necessary to carry out the purposes of this Declaration.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 4.6, Setbacks (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 8 of the recorded scan.

fact: The First Filing's covenants prohibit perimeter fences, require the committee's advance approval for any other fence and its location, and let the association order a nuisance pet kept within the fenced portion of its owner's lot.
quote: No building, fence, or other permanent structure shall be located on any lot without first obtaining the written consent of the Architectural Control Committee, approving the proposed location. … Any pet constituting a nuisance may be ordered by the Association to be kept within the fenced portion of its owner's lot, or ordered expelled from the subdivision. … No fence shall be erected on any lot within the Property except as approved in advance by the Architectural Control Committee. Perimeter fences are prohibited.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Secs. 3.2, 3.9 and 3.11 (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Pages 3 and 5 of the recorded scan. The October 2019 board minutes mention ACC fence guidelines being finalized; none are posted on the HOA site.

fact: The First Filing's covenants require committee approval for any exterior lighting and keep free-standing yard lights no higher than 12 feet above the ground.
quote: No exterior lighting shall be installed or maintained on any lot except as approved by the Architectural Control Committee. No free-standing yard light may be placed higher than twelve (12) feet above ground level.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 3.22, Outside Lighting (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 6 of the recorded scan. The same section requires each lot to keep one 60-watt light within five feet of the street burning through the hours of darkness.

fact: The First Filing's covenants bar any structure, planting or material in the platted utility, trail, landscaping and drainage easements that would interfere with utilities, change the flow of drainage channels or block trails, and let the association remove it at the owner's cost after 45 days' notice.
quote: Easements for the installation and maintenance of utilities, trails, landscaping, and drainage facilities are reserved as shown on the Plat, or those that may be recorded at a later date. Within these easements, no structure, planting or other materials shall be place or permitted which may damage or interfere with the installation and maintenance of utilities, which may change the direction of flow of drainage channels in the easements which hinders or obstructs the use of the trails system, or which adversely affects landscaping installed by the Developer. If any landscaping or structure is installed which violates such requirements, the Association may give the property owner written notice to remove such landscaping or structure within no less than forty-five (45) days after such notices is given, and if the owner fails to move the landscaping or structure within that time, the Association may have such work done at the expense of the owner of the Lot.
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 3.5, Easements (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 4 of the recorded scan.

fact: The First Filing's covenants require approved construction, which starts with the first substantial work including earthwork, to be finished within one year unless the committee reasonably agrees to more time.
quote: Once construction of any structure is commenced on any lot, with the prior approval of the Architectural Control Committee, such construction must be diligently continued and must be completed in accordance with the plans and specifications approved by the Architectural Control Committee, within one year of commencement, or such longer time reasonably consented to by the Architectural Control Committee, in light of the nature of the project or other mitigating factors. Commencement of construction shall be deemed to commence with the first substantial construction activity (including earth work).
source_label: Amended Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Boyd Lake Shores, First Filing, Sec. 3.19, Commencing and Finishing Construction (recorded April 11, 2002)
notes: Page 6 of the recorded scan.

fact: According to the First Filing board's October 2019 minutes, six lots belong to both the First and Second Filing associations, and the First Filing covenants do not apply to them.
quote: It should be noted that there is a total of 6 lots that are in Filing 1 HOA and Filing 2 HOA. Further, the 1st Filing HOA covenants do not apply to these six lots. … In short, the controlling documents of the 1st Filing HOA and Covenants allow the six lots to have all the benefits of 1st Filing amenities without following 1st Filing Covenants.
source_label: Boyd Lake Homeowners Association, First Filing, Board of Directors meeting minutes, October 15, 2019
notes: The item concerned one owner's dues request (name left out). The Second Filing's covenants were not found posted and were not read.

fact: Boyd Lake Shores' Third Filing association has its own Architecture Review Board, which asks owners planning home or landscaping changes to submit an online form with a detailed description and a lot layout well ahead of the work, and recommends talking with neighbors the changes would visually affect.
quote: Should you contemplate making changes to your home or landscaping please contact the Architectural Review Board to check for compliance with our Covenants and Bylaws. Please submit the on-line form below well ahead of scheduling any work to avoid possible delays while the ARB considers your requests. Please submit a detailed description of your planned improvements and a lot layout showing the location of these improvements. It is highly recommended that you discuss your plans with any neighbors who may be visually impacted by the changes proposed
source_label: Boyd Lake Shores HOA Third Filing website, Architecture Review Board page
notes: Linked from the First Filing site's Additional Filings page. The Third Filing's covenants were not read.

fact: Larimer County's Land Use Code, in the version effective December 8, 2025, exempts properties containing only single-unit detached, cabin or duplex dwellings from its landscaping section except the street landscaping, buffering and screening, and fences and walls standards.
quote: Properties containing only single-unit detached dwellings, cabin dwellings, or duplex dwellings are exempt from all parts of this section except for the following: 1. §4.7.4.D, Street Landscaping, 2. §4.8.1, Buffering and Screening; and 3. §4.8.2, Fences and Walls.
source_label: Larimer County Land Use Code, Article 4, Sec. 4.7.2.B, Landscaping exemptions (effective December 8, 2025)
notes: larimer.gov serves a bot challenge to plain curl; the PDF was retrieved through a fetch tool on 2026-09-26 and read in full with pdftotext (page 172). Re-check by hand.

fact: Larimer County's Land Use Code, effective December 8, 2025, prohibits nonfunctional artificial turf and permits functional artificial turf only in recreational or other civic, community or recreational spaces, or in engineered civil infrastructure, within its landscaping section.
quote: Functional artificial turf is only permitted in a recreational use area or other space regularly used for civic, community, or recreational purposes, or as a component of a product designed and approved by a professional engineer for civil infrastructure projects. Nonfunctional artificial turf is prohibited.
source_label: Larimer County Land Use Code, Article 4, Sec. 4.7.3.A.3.d, Turf, Functional and Nonfunctional Turf, and Artificial Turf Areas (effective December 8, 2025)
notes: Page 173. The same subsection bars nonfunctional cool-season turf on new development and redevelopment of commercial, civic, institutional and common interest properties and street rights-of-way. Section 4.7.2.B exempts single-unit detached properties from these standards (see luc-single-unit-exempt).

fact: Larimer County's building permit guide, updated August 7, 2026, requires permits for fences over 7 feet and retaining walls 4 feet or higher, exempts sheds up to 200 square feet, pergolas at least 67% open and decks no more than 30 inches above grade, and says setbacks and other code rules still apply to exempt work.
quote: Fences greater than 7 feet high … Retaining walls 4 feet or higher … Residential decks not more than 30” above grade at any point and that do not serve a required exit door … Accessory structures (storage shed, etc.) not greater than 200 square feet in floor area, provided a hazard is not created … Pergolas, arbors, or trellises whose roof area is at least 67% open. … Building and Land Use Code requirements, including but not limited to lot coverage, setbacks, and floodplain regulations, apply to structures exempt from building permits.
source_label: Larimer County Community Development, Building Permit Requirements: A Guide to Help Determine if a Building Permit is Required (updated 08/07/2026)
notes: The first two items are in the guide's 'Building Permit Required' column, the rest in 'Building Permit Not Required'. larimer.gov serves a bot challenge to plain curl; retrieved through a fetch tool and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-26.
